c.tagline: Palawan's laid-back gateway to an underground river and island-hopping paradise.

taxi.fareNote: A small fleet of metered taxis works the city center, but most short hops are by motorized tricycle at a set or negotiated fare. Grab coverage on the island is limited, so agree the fare first or ask your hotel to arrange a van.

emergency.note: 911 is the national emergency hotline covering police, fire, and medical.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Sabang: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park

avoid.reason: Minor pickpocketing in public markets and occasional tricycle overcharging are the main annoyances.

hood_desc: The walkable commercial heart along Rizal Avenue, near the Immaculate Conception Cathedral, Palawan Museum, Mendoza Park and the main tricycle routes; best for first-timers who want banks, tour offices and restaurants on the doorstep.

A coastal barangay about three kilometres south-east of downtown, fronting Puerto Princesa Bay at Canigaran Beach, with garden hotels, seafood places and the city resort; suits travellers who want to be by the water rather than in the town centre.

A quiet beach village about 50 km northwest, the jump-off for the UNESCO-listed Underground River and its zipline and mangrove tours; suits nature lovers who want to wake up by the sea and skip the town.

The northern coastal barangay, about 13 km up the North Road, where the Honda Bay island-hopping boats depart from the wharf; the barangay itself has almost no lodging, so the nearest beds are on the Honda Bay road in neighbouring Tagburos.

A calmer barangay a few kilometres north-east of the centre along the North Road national highway, with mid-range hotels, local eateries and easy tricycle access to town; suits budget and longer-stay travelers wanting a quieter base.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash on board - a few pesos for jeepneys and a set per-person fare for tricycles (agree it first for special or charter trips). Grab has limited coverage, so tricycles are the everyday way to get around.
transit.hours: Tricycles run from early morning until late night; jeepneys and vans thin out after dark, when tricycles and hotel transfers fill the gap.
transit.note: Puerto Princesa has no rail or metro. Getting around relies on the ubiquitous motorized tricycles for in-town trips, jeepneys and multicabs on set routes, and vans-for-hire for longer runs to Sabang (Underground River) or the north. Metered taxis exist but are limited and Grab coverage is patchy.

bus: San Jose Terminal (provincial buses & vans to El Nido, Roxas and Port Barton)
ferry: Port of Puerto Princesa (domestic ferries to Coron, Cuyo, Manila and Iloilo)

transit.m: Tricycle to the city center (10-15 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% for good service is appreciated. Many restaurants add a 10% service charge.

food.name: Crocodile sisig
food.desc: Chopped crocodile meat from the local farm, sizzled on a hot plate with onion, chilli and calamansi. Mild, chicken-like and the city signature dare.

places.name: Kinabuchs Grill and Bar
places.note: The city best-known grill bar and the standard address for crocodile sisig and beers.

places.name: Palawan Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Center

food.name: Tamilok
food.desc: Woodworm harvested from rotting mangrove trunks, eaten raw in vinegar and chilli like an oyster, or breaded and deep fried for beginners.

landmarks: Puerto Princesa Underground River
A UNESCO-listed subterranean river winding eight kilometres beneath a limestone mountain, paddled by lamplight past cathedral-like chambers of stalactites.
Honda Bay
An island-hopping playground of sandbars and coral gardens, where day-trippers snorkel with tropical fish off Starfish, Cowrie and Luli islands.
Immaculate Conception Cathedral
A striking powder-blue neo-Gothic cathedral on Rizal Avenue, standing on the site where Spanish colonists first celebrated mass in 1872.
Plaza Cuartel
A quiet memorial garden beside the cathedral preserving the ruins of a wartime garrison, honouring American POWs killed here in 1944.
Baker's Hill
A whimsical hilltop park of gardens, statues and a famous bakery, where visitors snack on hopia while enjoying breezy city views.
Mitra's Ranch
A breezy ranch estate on Santa Monica Heights offering ziplining, horseback rides and sweeping panoramas over Honda Bay.
Palawan Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Center
A conservation facility better known as the Crocodile Farm, breeding endangered Philippine crocodiles and sheltering bearcats, cockatoos and pythons.
Iwahig River Firefly Watching
An enchanting evening paddle through mangroves aglow with thousands of synchronised fireflies, with bioluminescent plankton sparkling beneath the boat.
Baywalk Park
The city's seaside promenade along Puerto Princesa Bay, buzzing at dusk with grilled-seafood stalls, joggers and pastel sunset skies.
Nagtabon Beach
A locals' favourite crescent of white sand and jade water tucked behind jungle hills, a 45-minute drive from downtown.

train.note: Palawan has no railway of any kind. All travel on the island is by road, boat or air, and Puerto Princesa's airport has direct flights from Manila, Cebu and some international destinations.

bus.note: No international coaches. The San Jose terminal north of the city is the hub for Palawan's north-south road: Cherry Bus and Roro Bus run to El Nido in about 5-6 hours and to Port Barton and Sabang for the Underground River. Shared vans are faster and leave when full. Buy at the terminal or through Biyaheroes; the road is now mostly paved but journeys still take longer than the map suggests.

intl.op: local bangka operators — tickets at Sta. Lourdes wharf

ferry.note: No international sailings. The 2GO ship to Manila takes the best part of a day and is the budget alternative to flying, running only a couple of times a week - check the schedule carefully. Coron is more usually reached by air or by the fast craft from El Nido than from Puerto Princesa. Honda Bay boats are island-hopping day trips rather than transport.

half.name: Balsahan River
half.blurb: Freshwater river and jungle trail in Iwahig, about 40 minutes south, runs through the grounds of a working penal colony.

half.name: Salakot Falls
half.blurb: Waterfall in the rural northern countryside, about 90 minutes away, is reached by a short forest trail through farmland.

half.name: Simpokan Beach
half.blurb: Undeveloped beach in northern Puerto Princesa, about two hours away, is often paired with a countryside waterfall tour.
